The code cells below are **interactive**. ::: {.callout-tip} ## How to Practice 1. **Click "Run Code"** to execute the code and see the result 2. **Edit the code directly** - change values and see what happens 3. **Experiment freely** - you can't break anything! ::: ### Types of Relationships Visualise positive, negative, and no relationship: ```{webr-r} # Positive relationship set.seed(42) x <- 1:20 y_pos <- x + rnorm(20, 0, 3) plot(x, y_pos, main = "Positive Relationship", xlab = "X", ylab = "Y", pch = 19, col = "steelblue") abline(lm(y_pos ~ x), col = "red", lwd = 2) ``` ::: {.callout-note} ## Challenge Change `y_pos <- x + rnorm(20, 0, 3)` to `y_neg <- -x + rnorm(20, 0, 3)` and update the plot to show a negative relationship. ::: ### Calculating r by Hand (Conceptually) ```{webr-r} x <- c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10) y <- c(3, 5, 4, 8, 9) r <- cor(x, y) cat("Correlation r =", round(r, 3), "\n\n") cat("Interpreting r =", round(r, 3), ":\n") if (abs(r) < 0.1) cat("Negligible relationship\n") else if (abs(r) < 0.3) cat("Small relationship\n") else if (abs(r) < 0.5) cat("Medium relationship\n") else cat("Large relationship\n") cat("Direction:", ifelse(r > 0, "Positive", "Negative")) ``` ### r² — Shared Variance ```{webr-r} r <- 0.70 r_squared <- r^2 cat("r =", r, "\n") cat("r² =", round(r_squared, 3), "\n\n") cat("Interpretation: The two variables share", round(r_squared * 100, 1), "% of their variance.\n\n") cat("The remaining", round((1 - r_squared) * 100, 1), "% of variance in Y is\nexplained by other factors.") ``` --- ## Self-Assessment Check your understanding before moving on. ::: {.webex-check .webex-box} **1.
